newsitem.title: USA: BP plans large increase in Alaska E&P budget.
newsitem.headline: BP plans large increase in Alaska E&P budget.

text.p: BP America Inc, a leading producer of Alaskan crude oil, is planning a substantial increase in its exploration and production budget for the state.
According to a state official, the Alaskan governor and executives of the BP Exploration Alaska Inc will announce an increase in capital spending here late Monday morning.

Earlier this week, Alaskan Governor Tony Knowles traveled to London to meet with executives of BP America's parent company, British Petroleum Co Plc, to discuss the increased investments in Alaska's North Slope (ANS) fields, the state official said.
BP owns about 43 percent of Alaska North Slope crude production, which has declined from over 2 million barrels daily in 1988 to 1.5 million in 1996.
BP currently plans to spend $2.5 billion over the next five years to develop North slope fields. Officials with BP declined to comment on their plans.
Recent success at new North Slope prospects, including BP's Northstar field, have prompted the governor to tout the state's more open business environment.

And Projects like BP's Northstar, slated for a 1999 production start and estimated to hold 130 million barrels of crude, have given industry observers hope that big oil can extend the lifespan of ANS production.
"(Oil companies) feel a combination of new technology and discoveries...will retard the rate of decline," said Bob Coleberd, a consultant with Pac West Oil Data in California.
